title: Pegula pulls out of Singapore after busy Hard-Court Swing
description: On the heels of her run to the US Open semifinals, Jessica Pegula will miss next week's Singapore Tennis Open. She is projected to return at the end of the month in Beijing.

body:
Jessica Pegula will miss next week's WTA 500 Singapore Tennis Open Presented by BNP Paribas, she announced on social media.

"I'm really disappointed to have to withdraw from Singapore," Pegula wrote in an Instagram story on Tuesday evening. "After a long and physically demanding few weeks at the US Open, I'm just not quite ready to get back on court and compete at the level I expect from myself.

"I was really looking forward to playing in Singapore and hope I can come back in the future ❤️"

It was quite a busy Hard-Court Swing for Pegula, currently at a career-high No. 3 in the PIF WTA Rankings.

She reached finals in Washington, D.C. and Cincinnati, with a run to the Round of 16 in Toronto sandwiched in between, before reaching the semifinals of the US Open for the second straight year.

The 32-year-old went 15-4 during the American Hard-Court Swing, and her 50 wins lead the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz. She's also currently third on the Race to the WTA Finals leaderboard, with 5,825 points.

Pegula is still scheduled to play the China Open, the first of back-to-back WTA 1000s, at the end of the month.

Pegula was going to be the top seed in Singapore. It will now be World No. 5 Mirra Andreeva. The 28-player field also includes Top 20 players Amanda Anisimova and Alexandra Eala. Maja Chwalinska, Elise Mertens, Barbora Krejcikova and Maria Sakkari will also be in the draw.

The Singapore Tennis Open and Korea Open, also being played next week, are the first two tournaments of the Asian Swing. They each kick off on Sept. 21 and will run through Sept. 27.

From there, the tour will head to Beijing for the China Open, beginning on Sept. 30 and concluding on Oct. 11.
author: Brad Kallet
